craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of fitted joinery — utsāha as qualifier meets qualified without loss. Kings retinue kept whole (horses/chariots/men — the three muster); double-grasp birth kept ablative per BOUNDARY. Rejected: (a) trimming retinue → killed: threefold muster is the showing. (b) genitive rival → killed: sense-equivalent, settled. Read aloud: EV-en IN-man-y-NESS, TWO-ness WOULD-be — … AS the KING's-HORS-es, CHAR-i-ots, MEN.

lines: Even in manyness, twoness would be —
born of double grasp — as the king's horses, chariots, men.

reads_against.argmap: Is there twoness in manyness? → Manyness still yields twoness, double-reflection-born — like the king's retinue.
c1_essence: Unity without strain for the consciousness-bodied; the worldly one's reflection-object fixed as difference-pithed non-difference-shining (vv10-11).
Mechanics: one thought un-touched, one word uniting many, helping relation admitted, twoness in manyness, two facings, three thinkings, genitive settling unself-lost (vv12-18).
